title: Winning Fulbright Fellowship Sample Essay: Personal Statement 2018
content:
I remember how dusty clouds of baking flour drifted while Polish words were spoken into the air. When I was young, my whole family baked holiday kołaczki (fruit-filled cookies) using recipes that were brought over from Poland. My grandmother, the one responsible for our family’s immigration to America, supervised as we kneaded the dough, breathing life into our heritage. These idyllic childhood scenes abruptly ended when my family hit rock-bottom nine years ago. The 2008 recession collapsed our real estate assets and triggered my family’s unraveling. After my parents’ divorce and my father’s departure, I took on the role of assisting my mother financially. The heroes that I once thought were flawless — my mother, my father, my extended family — all turned mortal before my eyes as they went their separate ways. These experiences, good and bad, inspire my application to the Fulbright ETA in Poland.

To support my family, I went to work after school. I managed a franchised business at 18 and became comfortable teaching in high-pressure environments. Every night after I closed the store, I did my homework in the kitchen office. This position funded the first semesters of my college education until I won a 2015 Gilman Scholarship to study in France. The Gilman Foundation taught me a lesson I had struggled to accept: despite my previously low self-esteem and the financial troubles my family faced, I was worth the investment. While abroad, I committed to personal development and professional networking. I volunteered in the urban community, registered for intellectual programs, and wrote my first novel. This text has been meticulously edited over the past two years and shares my transformative experiences through cultural exchange. Since living in France, I have continued to travel and have remained involved in the global community because of its ability to promote reflective discovery.

I credit the emotionally aware and ambidextrous thinker that I’ve become to my experiences abroad. These experiences were made possible by the teachers who gave me the confidence to cross my first language barrier. My formal international education truly started in French class in the U.S., when Mme. Caraballo not only taught me language skills, but also grew my global understanding. These skills allowed me to achieve my longstanding dream of better knowing my family’s background. This idea is at the core of my Fulbright application. I would like to not only teach English in Poland, but also to inspire my peers to pursue each of their goals with tenacity, as I have been taught to do.

My multicultural background has made me familiar with distinctly American traits and, my education makes me comfortable sharing these traits in diverse settings. Learning about other cultures helped me achieve my own goals; now, I would like to serve as the resource that supports Polish students to do the same. The staff at my school has invested in my personal and professional success and I would like to represent their work and our school through the Fulbright Program. Systematic differences create a gap in support networks for Polish students. I would like to close that gap. My past is evidence that teaching can absolutely change lives.

In Poland, I would like to use English lessons to promote leadership and post-graduate success, not just basic grammar. Teaching at the university level also offers a mix of English education, social studies, and collegiate thought, which I would like to use as structure for language lessons. As a graduating business strategy student who is looking to advance in the consulting industry, the Poland ETA would allow me to gain valuable experience in bringing out the best in people and their respective organizations.
